description:
Our team consists of three members: a PhD in Astrophysics, a Master’s degree in Planetary Sciences, and a Master’s degree in Medicine.

We're ready to monitor health of our astronauts!

Something's wrong? Well, let us know and we'll help you ASAP.
summary: Health Monitoring Software is a browser-based medical triage and crew health platform built for isolated missions where hospital access is unavailable. Designed to detect clinical issues early, it integrates physical symptom diagnostics, psychological screening, biometric vital analysis, and medical reference guides into one offline system. Users can evaluate symptoms across five anatomical layers (skin, blood, muscles, bones, and nerves) via a 3D body model to identify potential diseases and treatment protocols, or complete an eight-part clinical mental health assessment covering sleep, mood, and stress for targeted therapeutic advice. The platform supports live medical sensor input—simulated via CSV files in place of physical hardware—to run Fast Fourier Transform heart rate diagnostics and color-coded clinical range gauges for temperature, blood sugar, carbon dioxide, and oxygen. It also tracks solar radiation exposure risks on a yearly timeline and includes a direct Earth telemedicine link. Built with HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, HTML5 Canvas, SheetJS, and Mammoth.js, the project creatively turns complex clinical databases into visual diagnostic tools while allowing medical officers to update diseases, thresholds, and care guidelines using standard Excel, Word, and CSV files.
details:
What It Does and How It Works This project is an offline diagnostic and countermeasure system built for astronauts living and working in isolated, confined, and extreme spaceflight environments. It features a 90-question behavioral health assessment covering 7 space-specific themes (Sleep, Mood, Communication, Fun, Thoughts, Activities, Stress) and a general mental health screening module, scoring responses from 1 to 5 to provide 450 graduated solutions. It also includes a physiological symptom checker across 5 body systems (Skin, Blood, Muscles, Bones, Nerves) that links observed symptoms and biomarkers to 25 spaceflight conditions and NASA-grounded medical treatments.

Benefits and Intended Impact The system detects early physical and psychological strain before minor issues escalate into mission-critical emergencies. It enables crews to self-assess and apply immediate countermeasures autonomously during deep-space missions where communication delays prevent real-time guidance from Mission Control. It reduces stigma by providing private, non-punitive self-monitoring that encourages timely Flight Surgeon or behavioral health support.

Data Sources and Hardware Medical and psychological protocols are built from NASA Human Research Program (HRP) research, International Space Station (ISS) medical checklists, and Mental Health America (MHA) screening frameworks. The system is structured as lightweight, offline Excel spreadsheets designed to run directly on standard crew tablets or spacecraft laptops without requiring constant ground telemetry.

Creativity The system uniquely pairs moderate-to-critical psychological interventions (levels 3 to 5) with targeted music therapy recommendations calibrated by tempo (BPM) and acoustic texture to help regulate the nervous system. It brings aerospace medicine and behavioral psychology together into a single unified mind-body workflow rather than treating them separately.

Key Factors Considered We accounted for space-specific stressors including the 90-minute orbital light-dark cycle, sensory monotony, microgravity fluid shifts, radiation exposure, and interpersonal friction in confined quarters. We organized interventions into graduated escalation tiers so mild symptoms are managed through simple self-regulation while severe conditions trigger clinical care and operational safeguards.
